info.label: Columbia
info.desc: "The Wall" is the eleventh studio album by the English rock band Pink Floyd, released on 30 November 1979 by Harvest/EMI and Columbia/CBS Records. A rock opera, it follows the character Pink, a disillusioned rock star who builds a psychological “wall” of social isolation. The album topped the United States charts for 15 weeks and reached number three in the United Kingdom. Initially met with mixed reviews, with some critics describing it as overblown and pretentious, it has since been acclaimed as one of the greatest albums of all time. podcast.body: The concept for this album began to form in Roger Waters' mind in 1977, driven by his frustration with performing in large stadiums where audiences seemed more interested in beer than the music. He proposed the idea to the rest of Pink Floyd in 1978. The album served as the basis for the 1980 tour, during which a massive brick wall was gradually constructed on stage throughout the first half of the show, symbolizing the "growing isolation" felt by the burned-out rock star protagonist, Pink. "The wall was born out of the frustration that Roger Waters felt about performing in large stadiums. He started thinking about it in 1977 and proposed it to the rest of Pink Floyd in 1978."

This album has achieved sales exceeding 50 million copies worldwide. Curiously, even with such high sales, it has not received a "Uranium record," indicating an inconsistency in the criteria for these special awards.
